In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our data demonstrate that IgA memory B cell responses can be detected in peripheral blood after vaccination with a mucosal vaccine.
we have established a novel approach for detection of vaccine specific memory responses.
we have demonstrated that the inactivated oral vaccine Dukoral induces IgA memory B cell responses and that these IgA memory B-cell responses are maintained at least for 9 months.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have established an in vitro assay for the detection of mucosal vaccine specific IgA(+) B cells and demonstrated that this approach can be used for the assessment of mucosal vaccine responses in humans.

we have identified a method for in vitro differentiation of vaccine specific Ig memory B cells and that we have demonstrated the presence of vaccine specific memory B cells for at least 3 months after immunization.
the combination of immunostimulatory CpG oligonucleotide, BAFF, IL-15, and the oral cholera vaccine, Dukoral, is a novel and useful tool for assessment of mucosal immune responses.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the in vitro stimulation of IgA memory cells with immunostimulating DNA, BAFF and IL-15 provides a novel approach to assess the magnitude and longevity of IgA-mediated immune responses induced by oral vaccines and may be of value for other mucosal vaccines.

stimulation of IgA memory cells with BAFF, immunostimulatory oligonucleotides and IL-15 provides a novel approach to assess mucosal vaccine specific memory B cells and to investigate mechanisms of long-term IgA responses.

stimulation of IgA memory cells by immunostimulatory DNAs in combination with BAFF and IL-15 can be used to detect vaccine specific IgA-secre ting cells and to study long-term memory responses to mucosally delivered vaccines.
